answer: The bridge chain is checked at intake, gaps appear in pulse, and relic seals the repaired sequence, which the replay verifies against each signature. Cloning a key into 30 hands breaks the sequence as two signers race the same nonce, thus a shared-credential farm convicts itself on the first collision. Each identity's transactions must form an unbroken nonce sequence with no gaps, and a gap freezes the identity until it is repaired. That is 7 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
